short: William Shakespeare was an English playwright, poet, and actor, widely regarded as the greatest writer in the English language.
full:
Born in Stratford-upon-Avon, William Shakespeare established his career in London's thriving Elizabethan theatre scene. He became a leading member and part-owner of the Lord Chamberlain's Men, writing a steady stream of acclaimed comedies, histories, and early tragedies. By the late 1590s, his company had built the Globe Theatre on the south bank of the Thames, where masterpieces like *Hamlet* and *Macbeth* were eventually performed.

Shakespeare's surviving body of work—including 39 plays and 154 sonnets—profoundly shaped English literature and the language itself. His extraordinary ability to capture the breadth of human emotion and conflict transcended his own era. Though he died in 1616, the publication of the First Folio in 1623 ensured the survival of his plays, securing his enduring global legacy.
